Figure 1. Cyclopropanol rings. (A) Cyclopropanol ring opening
mediated by a single-electron reduction. (B) Structures of known
natural products that contain a cyclopropanol moiety. (C) Structural
similarity (blue) between D-cleonine, L-cleonine, and trigonic acid.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthesis pathway to the cyclopropanol-containing
malleicyprol polyketides. The bur biosynthetic gene cluster (36 kbp in
size) is responsible for the biosynthesis of the malleicyprols.
L-
Methionine is converted to cyclopropanol-containing trigonic acid via
DMSP. Trigonic acid is then used as a building block to produce the
virulence-conferring cyclopropanol group of the malleicyprols.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Biosynthesis of valgamicin C. (A) Model of the biosynthetic pathway for valgamicin C. Domain abbreviations: (A) Adenylation; (C)
condensation; (E) epimerization; (KR) ketoreductase; (nMT) N-methyltransferase; (T) thiolation; (TE) thioesterase. (B) The adenylation (A)
domains of ValAIII and ValA both lack the conserved Asp in the A4 motifposition highlighted with a (*), indicating they adenylate a nonamino
acid. The sequence of the GrsA A domain from the gramicidin S biosynthesis pathway (which contains an Asp) is included for comparison.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Isotopic labeling of valgamicin C. (A) The valgamicin producer, Amycolatopsis sp. ML1-hF4 was cultured with DMSP (top) or
DMSP−13C3 (bottom). The cultures were then extracted and analyzed by HPLC-HRMS. Displayed are the extracted [M + H]+ ion
chromatograms of each of the four valgamicins. The addition of DMSP−13C3 to the Amycolatopsis sp. ML1-hF4 fermentation medium resulted in
the +3 u labeling of valgamicin C (calcd 626.3751, found 626.3742 Δ 1.44 ppm). (B) Addition of 124 μM DMSP to the Amycolatopsis sp. ML1-
hF4 culture medium selectively increases the production of valgamicin C relative to the other valgamicins. (n = 3, unpaired t test: ***p < 0.001).
(C) The addition of L-methionine-13C5-15N to the Amycolatopsis sp. ML1-hF4 fermentation medium also resulted in the selective +3 u labeling of
valgamicin C. The +3 u [M + H]+ mass at 626.3752 corresponds to valgamicin C−13C3 (calcd 626.3751, found 626.3752 Δ 0.16 ppm). (D)
Extracted ion chromatograms demonstrating the production of DMSP, gonyol, and gonydiol in the Amycolatopsis sp. ML1-hF4. References used:
commercial DMSP, synthetic racemic gonyol, synthetic racemic anti-gonydiol.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Trigonic acid operon in other bacterial species. (A) The
production of gonyol from the trigonic acid operon-containing species
Nocardiopsis chromatogenes, Micromonospora nigra, S. mobaraensis, and
Nitrospirillium iridis. (B) Extracted ion chromatograms of trigonic acid
produced by S. mobaraensis. (C) Purification of SUMO-MobG, the
BurG homologue from S. mobaraensis. (D) In vitro activity assay of
SUMO-MobG converting gonydiol to trigonic acid. References used:
synthetic racemic gonyol, synthetic racemic gonydiol, and synthetic
racemic trigonic acid. (E) Bayesian phylogenetic tree made using the
ketosynthase sequences from the BurA homologues. Escherichia coli
and Streptomyces avermitilis FabH enzymes used as the outgroups.
